findings.what: Public WorkflowRunner still converts absent/non-callable handlers to no-ops and can durably complete P0-P7 without production artifacts.
findings.why: The fail-open test seam remains a public competing execution entry despite run_workflow's fail-closed composition.

findings.what: Changed-source recovery is not executable through the advertised dispatcher; existing source records suppress input pause but reuse stale registration, while replacement input is rejected as duplicate.
findings.why: The public production mutation path cannot resume the earliest affected suffix and tests hide this with injected no-op handlers.

findings.what: Gate B identity is assigned to P6 although Gate B follows completed P6 and precedes P7.
findings.why: Gate B receipt changes unnecessarily invalidate replay/review instead of preserving P6 and reopening the Gate B/P7 boundary.

findings.what: write_report writes README complete/P7 before chart generation and before WorkflowRunner commits P7.
findings.why: A chart failure can leave authoritative state unavailable while user-visible README says complete, retaining a second state writer.

findings.what: workflow.py is now a 922-line module combining storage, retries, invalidation, hashing, input schemas, gate policy, and production handlers.
findings.why: This exceeds the maintainability size/single-responsibility guidance; separate composition/input policy after blockers without adding a framework.

evidence.output: Gate APIs are artifact-only and detector receipt authorization is phase-independent; public WorkflowRunner no-op, source reacquisition, GateB mapping, and README completion remain.
711 passed; tests do not cover the blockers.
